messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'prod-gpu-1' reaching capacity threshold. queue_length=842, avg_wait=42s, throttled_requests=129. autoscaler_error='scale_limit_reached'
ryan (oncall): seeing the alert. I'm paged, taking it.
ryan (oncall): reading autoscaler logs now — looks like we've hit the max_nodes limit for that pool and MIG slices are highly fragmented.
maria (SRE): confirmed. MIG allocation imbalance: a bunch of 1g.5gb slices scattered, can't pack 8g jobs.
alex (ML infra): queue is mostly long-running chat-generation jobs pinned to 8g. Need to either migrate to 4g-quantized variant or free contiguous MIG capacity.
tanvi (Platform): what was recent change? any rollout that touched pool sizing?
ryan (oncall): no recent rollout. Policy bump last week increased min_scale for another cluster, but this pool's max_nodes is 40 and we've got 40 nodes active.
liz (Customer Success): heads-up — we've seen a spike in customer tickets referencing latency and 429s. Top-affected tenant: Acme.ai (high traffic) — flagged.
mike (eng-oncall): I'm on standby to help with rapid config changes. If we need a temporary uplift to max_nodes I can submit.
ryan (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) emergency increase pool max_nodes +25 for 30m; 2) trigger best-effort rebalance to defragment MIG slices; 3) temporarily route new 8g jobs to fallback model-4g-quant; 4) notify customers. Opinions?
maria (SRE): +1. Rebalance can be disruptive if we don't coordinate cooldown windows. We should prioritize draining lowest-priority jobs.
alex (ML infra): I can flip routing for new requests to model-4g-quant via feature flag. That reduces new pressure but doesn't clear the queue.
tanvi (Platform): I can apply the max_nodes bump. Need approval from ops lead — mike can you approve?
mike (eng-oncall): approved. go ahead tanvi.
tanvi (Platform): running command now:
```bash
platformctl pools update prod-gpu-1 --max-nodes 65 --temp-ttl 30m
```

incident-bot: action acknowledged: pool max_nodes set to 65 (temp ttl 30m) by tanvi.
ryan (oncall): starting rebalance plan: mark low-priority jobs for preemption, drain nodes with smallest available contiguous MIG slices first. Maria, can you start drain list?
maria (SRE): creating node drain list now. I'll tag nodes with a 'rebalance-drain' annotation and start evicting pods.
alex (ML infra): routing switch ready. Will flip the flag in 30s to cut new 8g arrivals.
liz (Customer Success): drafting an external note: short blurb explaining transient throttling and mitigation steps. Will share once we have ETA.
ryan (oncall): flip now?
alex (ML infra): flipping flag: 
```json
{"routes":{"/v1/generate":{"model_fallback":"model-4g-quant","condition":"new_requests_only"}}}
```

alex (ML infra): routing change live. New heavy requests should now go to 4g-quant fallback.
r yan (oncall): typo in my last message. ignore.
maria (SRE): eviction progress: 65% nodes drained for targeted set. Some pods are rescheduling onto nodes we intend to drain — adding taints.
tanvi (Platform): confirmed more capacity appearing: free_mig_slices=12 contiguous 8g ready. Queue length dropping to 412. avg_wait=18s.
liz (Customer Success): updating ticket for Acme.ai: "We experienced transient throttling due to GPU pool capacity and autoscaler limits. We've expanded capacity and are rebalancing to restore normal latency. Will follow up with postmortem."
mike (eng-oncall): I see instance churn. Any risk to per-tenant isolation during rebalance?
maria (SRE): low. We're preferring preempt from best-effort pools first; production-traffic only from selected nodes.
ryan (oncall): small gotcha: one node failed to drain (stuck in Terminating). Logs show CSI attach/detach timeout causing pod eviction hang.
maria (SRE): hitting known bug — reattach timeouts during heavy NIC attach. I'll escalate to infra to force detach.
tanvi (Platform): issuing force detach on node-17: `kubectl annotate node node-17 critical-detach=true` then `platformctl node force-detach node-17`

incident-bot: action logged: force detach issued on node-17 by tanvi.
maria (SRE): node-17 freed, drain completed. More contiguous MIG slices now available. queue_length=198, avg_wait=6s. throttled_requests down to 14.
ryan (oncall): good. monitor for the next 15m until temp max_nodes TTL expires. If backlog still >100 we'll extend.
alex (ML infra): note — fallback to 4g-quant may produce slightly different outputs. Ops: we should add a short 'degraded-quality' header to explain fallback when applicable.
liz (Customer Success): I'll add that to the customer note.
mike (eng-oncall): any permanent fix suggestions?
maria (SRE): long term: tighten binpacking heuristics, allow hot rebin across MIG slices, and revisit default MIG sizes for this pool. Also consider raising burst limit and auto-adjusting max_nodes during sustained spikes.
tanvi (Platform): filed task PLAT-876: "Analyze prod-gpu-1 MIG sizing & binpacking; propose migration to 8g-aligned node types". Assigned to tanvi + alex. ETA EOW.
ryan (oncall): immediate follow-ups: - extend temp max_nodes by 30m if queue >100 at TTL - produce incident summary + timeline in incidents channel - coordinate with CS for affected customers

liz (Customer Success): shared update to Acme.ai and three other customers. They've acknowledged. No escalations to execs so far.
maria (SRE): monitoring shows stable. throttled_requests=0, queue_length=21. good to start cooling down.
ryan (oncall): starting cooldown: revert any aggressive taints/evictions, allow normal scheduling.
tanvi (Platform): scheduled TTL expiry still at +12m. I'll proactively set it to expire in 10m.

incident-bot: NOTICE: temp max_nodes TTL set to expire at 3305124060.
ryan (oncall): handing off to maria for post-incident work and timeline. I'm going offline for the next hour.
maria (SRE): taking ownership for post-incident. will collect logs, attach autoscaler traces, and write a draft postmortem.
liz (Customer Success): will follow up with customers tomorrow with summary and remediation plan.
mike (eng-oncall): thumbs. :thumbsup:

maria (SRE): ACTIONS: ["Collect autoscaler logs","Gather MIG allocation snapshots pre/post","Evaluate binpacking heuristics","Draft customer impact summary"]

alex (ML infra): adding an action: "Add runtime flag to mark 4g-quant fallback in response headers". Filed INFRA-342.

ryan (oncall): thanks all. Closing thread for live mitigation. Please ping me if anything regresses. :pray:
